title: Surface Modeling and Curvature Analysis Tool — Overview and definition
t: Surface Modeling and Curvature Analysis Tool — Overview and definition
description: Builds Class-A surfaces and analyzes curvature continuity for quality.
body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Builds Class-A surfaces and analyzes curvature continuity for quality. A surface modeling and curvature analysis tool creates NURBS patches with G0/G1/G2 continuity and visualizes Gaussian and mean curvature, zebra stripes, and reflection lines. Real implementations include Rhino/Grasshopper, Alias, and the surfacing modules of CATIA/NX. It detects inflections, flat spots, and continuity breaks before tooling is cut.
capabilities: NURBS surface creation, blending, and fairing
Curvature combs, zebra, and environment-map analysis
G0/G1/G2 continuity checking across patch boundaries
Automatic repair of gaps and tangent breaks
Export of watertight Class-A surfaces to CAD

body: Signature edition. Signature-original methods and framings for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. Teaching ladder for Surface Modeling and Curvature Analysis Tool, simple to complex. Rank 1: name the tool's single core action (NURBS surface creation, blending, and fairing). Rank 3: run it once on a tiny input and check the output. Rank 5: combine two capabilities: NURBS surface creation, blending, and fairing and Curvature combs, zebra, and environment-map analysis. Rank 7: chain its output into a neighboring tool (3D CAD modeling program) with a verification checkpoint. Rank 9+: automate the full workflow and teach it to someone else.
